findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: The paper gives total investments of £68.75m at 30 September 2026, but its portfolio table totals £75.12m and is headed 30 September 2025.
findings.detail: The portfolio table totals £75.12m and is labelled as at 30 September 2025. The paper also cites short-term deposits of £42.75m as at 30 September 2025, which the text describes as the position at 30 September 2025 rather than 2026.
findings.matters: A reader checking treasury figures needs one consistent investment total and a clear reporting date.
findings.figures: £68.75m total investments (30 September 2026 text); £75.12m portfolio table total; £42.75m short-term deposits (labelled 30 September 2025)

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: The authority has operated within its approved limits in the financial year to date.
findings.detail: The paper says the authorised limits in Appendix 1 are set above the capital financing requirement to allow the treasury manager to respond to advice. It states that the authority has been operating within those limits.
findings.matters: Finance officers at other councils will want to see confirmation that prudential limits are being kept to during the year.

findings.quote: In the financial year to date, the Authority has been operating within the approved limits.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: The PWLB certainty rate for 10-year loans rose from 5.62% to 6.17% over the period, and short-term rates are above long-term rates.
findings.detail: Rates for 20-year loans moved from 6.13% to 6.61% and 50-year loans from 6.01% to 6.37%. Short-term borrowing from other local authorities cost 3.8% to 5.5%, and the paper says short-term rates are higher than long-term rates at present.
findings.matters: Any council that repays a loan and replaces the funding will face the cost of PWLB or market funding at these rates, so a lender or finance director will want the rate path.
findings.figures: 10-year PWLB certainty rate 5.62% to 6.17%; 20-year 6.13% to 6.61%; 50-year 6.01% to 6.37%; short-term local authority borrowing 3.8% to 5.5%
findings.quote: The PWLB certainty rate for 10-year maturity loans was 5.62% at the beginning of the period and 6.17% at the end.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: Capital expenditure is forecast to underspend the approved programme, which the paper attributes to delays in certain capital projects.
findings.detail: The paper refers to the Capital Monitoring Quarter Two report for the project-level detail. It does not give the size of the underspend in this report.
findings.matters: A finance director tracking slippage across councils will want to know which programmes are underspending and why.
findings.figures: None stated in this paper
findings.quote: shows that there will be an underspend on the approved capital programme.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: The projected capital financing requirement falls from £342.254m at 31 March 2026 to £336.904m at 31 March 2027.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the budgeted decrease to the annual minimum revenue provision (MRP) and to changes in the timing and financing of the capital programme, including slippage in borrowing-funded expenditure.
findings.matters: A finance director comparing the underlying borrowing need with peers will want the CFR movement and its stated causes.
findings.figures: £342.254m actual CFR (31 March 2026); £336.904m projected CFR (31 March 2027)
findings.quote: Appendix 1 shows a projected CFR value of £336.904m as at the 31st of March 2027, compared with an actual CFR of £342.254m as at 31st March 2026.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: Investment balances are lower than the budget assumed because reserves have been used, and the paper says higher investment rates have offset this.
findings.detail: The paper says the shortfall in balances has been offset by investment rates remaining higher than those assumed when the budget was set. No amount is given for the reserves drawn down.
findings.matters: Finance directors tracking reserve use will want to see whether drawdowns are being absorbed by treasury income or are reducing the investment base.
findings.figures: None stated in the paper for the reserves drawn down or the balance shortfall
findings.quote: Whilst investment balances have been lower than originally assumed due to the utilisation of reserves

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: Caerphilly reports a 4.62% total income return on £68.75m of investments at 30 September 2026, against a 3.75% target.
findings.detail: The target was the Bank Rate in place when the strategy was set, and Bank Rate held at 3.75% through the period. The paper says investments in pooled funds, which it intends to hold for at least five years, generated an income return of 5%.
findings.matters: A finance director comparing treasury returns with peers will want the reported return against the benchmark rate the strategy used.
findings.figures: 4.62% total income return; £68.75m investments; 3.75% target; 5% pooled fund income return
findings.quote: The total investments held as at 30th September 2026 were £68.75m and had a total income rate of return equating to 4.62%.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: Total debt outstanding at 30 September 2026 is £270.8m, made up of £235.2m of PWLB loans, £10m of market loans (LOBOs), £23.8m of Welsh Government loans and £1.8m of a Salix loan.
findings.detail: The paper lists £10m of market loans (LOBOs) within total debt at 30 September 2026. It does not report a lender option being exercised, or a repayment, on those loans in the period.
findings.matters: A lender or finance officer looking at council debt exposure will want the composition of the portfolio, including the LOBO holding.
findings.figures: £270.8m total debt; £235.2m PWLB; £10m LOBOs; £23.8m Welsh Government; £1.8m Salix
findings.quote: The total debt outstanding as at 30th September 2026 was £270.8m and comprised of £235.2m PWLB loans; £10m market loans (LOBOs)

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Quarter Two Monitoring Report (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026).
findings.headline: No external borrowing took place in the reported period, with the internal borrowing position at £54.8m as at 31 March 2026.
findings.detail: The authority has operated a policy of internal borrowing to reduce risk and keep interest costs low. Borrowing is planned for 2026/27 for the General Fund and HRA capital programmes, but none had taken place by 30 September 2026.
findings.matters: A finance director deciding when to replace internally held funding with external debt will want to see how long a council has deferred borrowing and at what cost.
findings.figures: £54.8m internal borrowing (31 March 2026); £0 external borrowing in the period
findings.quote: during the reported period no external borrowing has taken place

findings.headline: 71% of Caerphilly's fixed rate borrowing matures in over 10 years, and 3% matures within 12 months.
findings.detail: The maturity structure table gives the actual split of fixed rate borrowing across maturity bands. The over-10-years band is the largest by a wide margin.
findings.matters: A profile this concentrated in long maturities means little refinancing falls due in the short term, which bears on the council's refinancing risk.
findings.figures: Over 10 years: £205,162k (71%). Under 12 months: £9,206k (3%). Over 12 months and within 24 months: £11,448k (4%).

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated investments at 2026-27 year-end are £68.8m, against a budgeted £50.0m.
findings.detail: The paper sets the estimate for principal outstanding on investments above budget. The budget for investments over 364 days is £60.0m, and the paper gives the same figure for the estimate.
findings.matters: Holding more cash than budgeted while borrowing is lower than budgeted is a combination a finance director and a lender would both want to see.
findings.figures: Principal outstanding on investments: budget £50,000k, estimate £68,750k. Upper limit for investments over 364 days: £60,000k.
findings.quote: Principal outstanding on investments 50,000 68,750

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated financing costs are 1.84% of net revenue stream for the General Fund, against a budgeted 2.08%, and 15.11% for the HRA, against 17.06%.
findings.detail: The ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream is reported for both funds. Both estimates sit below budget, and the HRA figure is the higher of the two.
findings.matters: This ratio is the standard measure of how much of the revenue budget goes on servicing debt, so a peer or lender can compare the position directly.
findings.figures: General Fund total financing costs: budget £10,434k, estimate £9,237k, against net revenue stream of £502,559k. HRA total: budget £10,803k, estimate £9,565k, against net revenue stream of £63,322k.
findings.quote: Total as percentage of net revenue stream 2.08% 1.84%

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated unsupported HRA borrowing for 2026-27 is £16.1m, against £31.0m budgeted and £44.7m in the revised budget.
findings.detail: The funding table shows unsupported HRA borrowing falling from the revised budget to the estimate. General Fund unsupported borrowing also falls, from £6.5m revised to an estimated £1.4m.
findings.matters: Unsupported borrowing is funded by the council itself, so a fall in its estimated use shows how much new debt it expects to take on for the housing programme.
findings.figures: Unsupported Borrowing HRA: budget £31,000k, revised budget £44,746k, estimate £16,086k. Unsupported Borrowing (General Fund): budget £11,892k, revised budget £6,467k, estimate £1,440k.
findings.quote: Unsupported Borrowing HRA 31,000 44,746 16,086

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated capital expenditure for 2026-27 is £168.3m, against a budget of £195.0m, with HRA expenditure estimated at £64.8m against £94.8m budgeted.
findings.detail: The capital table shows Council Fund spending estimated at £103.5m against a budget of £100.2m, while HRA spending is estimated well below budget. The paper's revised budget column for the total is £202.0m.
findings.matters: A large HRA underspend against budget affects the timing of council housing borrowing and the grant and reserve funding behind it, which is relevant to lenders and to peers planning similar programmes.
findings.figures: Total expenditure: budget £195,031k, revised budget £202,000k, estimate £168,313k. Council Fund: budget £100,190k, estimate £103,505k. HRA: budget £94,841k, estimate £64,808k.
findings.quote: Housing Revenue Account 94,841 93,468 64,808

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated Capital Financing Requirement at 2026-27 year-end is £336.9m, against a budgeted £404.9m.
findings.detail: The paper reports the Capital Financing Requirement for the Council Fund and the HRA separately, with the total estimated below budget. The Council Fund estimate is £208.2m against a budget of £252.9m, and the HRA estimate is £128.7m against £152.0m.
findings.matters: The CFR is the council's underlying need to borrow, so a finance officer at another council can compare the gap between CFR and actual borrowing with their own.
findings.figures: CFR total: budget £404,900k, estimate £336,904k. Council Fund: budget £252,900k, estimate £208,166k. HRA: budget £152,000k, estimate £128,738k.
findings.quote: Capital Financing Requirement 404,900 336,904

findings.headline: Caerphilly's estimated outstanding borrowing at 2026-27 year-end is £287.7m, against a budgeted £425.1m.
findings.detail: The mid-year report sets the budgeted outstanding borrowing against the estimate for the same year. Estimated net debt is £231.8m against a budgeted £384.0m.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender can see that the council expects to hold roughly £137m less borrowing than its budget assumed, which changes how much new funding it needs to raise.
findings.figures: Outstanding borrowing: budget £425,081k, estimate £287,676k. Net debt: budget £384,008k, estimate £231,811k.
findings.quote: Outstanding Borrowing 425,081 287,676

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: The Housing Revenue Account projects a £1.506m underspend, about 2% of its total budget
findings.detail: The paper says the underspend mainly comes from employee costs and non-pay budgets, including £1.058m within Housing Strategy projects due to phasing. Building Maintenance and Response Repairs are projected to overspend by £1.576m.
findings.matters: A ringfenced HRA underspend that offsets repairs demand pressure shows how HRA working balances are being used to support capital delivery.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: The medium-term plan gap for 2027/28 and 2028/29 was £8.457m in the base case at budget setting, and £28.712m in the downside case
findings.detail: The paper says the MTFP will be updated to include 2029/30 and that current trends show demand and cost growth exceeding available resources in several service areas. It identifies ALN, social care, temporary accommodation and home to school transport as the most significant emerging pressures.
findings.matters: The gap is a cumulative figure under three funding scenarios, so it indicates how sensitive the medium-term position is to council tax and grant assumptions.
findings.figures: £8.457m base-case cumulative budget gap for 2028/29; £2.205m best case; £28.712m worst case; £8.457m gap for the following two years at budget setting

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Library savings of £0.119m in 2026/27 are rated Red while a Court of Appeal decision on the judicial review is awaited
findings.detail: The paper says the High Court refused the claimant permission on 14 August 2026, so the Council's decision stands. An appeal is now before the Court of Appeal, and the total savings profile for the library strategy is £0.477m across 2026/27 to 2028/29.
findings.matters: A saving tied to a live judicial review, with the appeal still pending, is a delivery risk that other councils planning service closures could face.
findings.figures: £0.119m of 2026/27 library savings rated Red; £0.477m total savings profile across 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: an appeal now sits at the Court of Appeal where we await a decision

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: 2026/27 pay awards of 3.3% for NJC staff and 3.5% for teachers add an unbudgeted £0.946m against a 3% budgeted provision
findings.detail: The paper says the awards exceed the budgeted provision and add to in-year pressure on service budgets. It says Welsh Government grant for teachers' pay partly offsets the additional cost.
findings.matters: Pay awards above the budgeted provision are a common 2026/27 pressure, and the offset from specific grant shows one way councils are covering it.
findings.figures: £0.946m unbudgeted cost; 3% budgeted pay provision; 3.3% NJC award; 3.5% teachers award
findings.quote: have resulted in an additional unbudgeted cost of £0.946m

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Social Services projects a £2.054m overspend, and a draw on its demand risk reserve may be requested at outturn
findings.detail: The paper says the projection rose from £1.163m at quarter one to £2.054m, as demand for long-term care increased. Children's Services is projected to overspend £0.567m and Adult Services £1.759m, partly offset by Business Support.
findings.matters: A call on a dedicated demand reserve at outturn is a specific, testable step that finance officers elsewhere face when social care demand outruns budget.
findings.figures: £2.054m net Social Services overspend; £1.163m quarter one potential overspend; £0.567m Children's Services overspend; £1.759m Adult Services overspend; £0.271m Business Support underspend

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: 28 schools requested to set deficit budgets for 2026/27 with a cumulative value of £8.87 million, and 11 have submitted recovery plans that support sign-off
findings.detail: The paper says the deficit requests include £1.98 million for St Martins Comprehensive and £3.64 million for YG Cwm Rhymni. It notes there is a current consultation on YG Cwm Rhymni.
findings.matters: Licensed deficits approved against recovery plans are a route other councils use to manage school budgets, and their scale here is set out in full.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Schools' projected collective deficit is £4.543m at 31 March 2027, against £4.526m at budget setting
findings.detail: The paper says 31 schools are projected to be in deficit, with a combined value of £9.5m. It also says the continuing deterioration in school balances points to structural pressures, which are being considered by the Sustainable Communities for Learning Working Group.
findings.matters: Falling pupil numbers and surplus places driving school deficits is a pressure other councils face, and it can end up on the council's own balance sheet.
findings.figures: £4.543m projected collective deficit at 31 March 2027; £4.526m at budget setting; 31 schools in deficit; £9.5m value of those schools' deficits

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Capital Finance forecasts a £1.154m underspend from a lower MRP charge after capital programme slippage
findings.detail: The paper says slippage reduced the Minimum Revenue Provision and the immediate need to borrow, which lowered interest payable. It describes the change as a significant improvement in the Capital Finance budget position.
findings.matters: Slippage that cuts MRP and borrowing costs in-year is a recurring pattern that lenders and peers can use to judge how capital delivery affects the revenue position.
findings.figures: £1.154m net underspend
findings.quote: Capital Finance is currently forecasting a net underspend of £1.154m.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Transformation savings target underachievement is projected at £1.267m against the £5.581m target
findings.detail: The £5.581m target was allocated to services, except £3.467m held under Miscellaneous Finance for management restructure, workforce planning and commercially sensitive projects. The paper says savings projects are being reviewed for deliverability.
findings.matters: Transformation targets are the main recurring-savings lever in many councils' medium-term plans, so a mid-year shortfall is a signal other finance officers can benchmark.
findings.figures: £5.581m Transformation savings target; £1.267m projected overspend; £3.467m held under Miscellaneous Finance
findings.quote: At quarter two, there is a projected overspend of £1.267m resulting from the underachievement of savings targets.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: £2.456m of the £12.332m 2026/27 savings are assessed as having significant deliverability risk and are reported as overspends
findings.detail: £4.039m of savings are assessed as fully achieved at 30 September 2026 and £5.359m are forecast to be achieved by year end. The paper says leadership is identifying mitigating actions and alternative efficiencies.
findings.matters: The share of savings flagged Red at mid-year shows how much of a budget built on savings is at risk of becoming an overspend.
findings.figures: £12.332m total savings; £4.039m blue (fully achieved); £5.359m green; £0.479m amber; £2.456m red
findings.quote: £ 2.456m savings have been assessed as having significant deliverability risk

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter Two).
findings.headline: Quarter two projects a 2026/27 revenue overspend of £2.623m, an improvement of £0.244m on quarter one
findings.detail: The forecast combines actuals to 30 September 2026 with projections for the full year. The paper says the improvement masks increased pressures in Education and Social Services and in Housing and Environment, offset by improvements elsewhere.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the size and direction of a mid-year movement against the same pressures in social care, transport and homelessness.

findings.quote: The quarter two forecast shows a projected revenue overspend of £2.623m for 2026/27, an improvement of £0.244m since quarter one.

findings.headline: Bryn Carno, Rhymney shows £79,289 spent and forecast against a nil revised budget, a £79,289 overspend
findings.detail: The scheme has no revised budget for 2026/27, but £79,289 has been spent to end Q2 and the same amount is forecast. The table records the variance as a £79,289 overspend.
findings.matters: A scheme running spend with no budget line is a control point a finance director would want to see reconciled, and other councils with similar unbudgeted schemes would find it relevant.
findings.figures: Revised budget £0 (shown as nil); actual to end Q2 £79,289; forecast £79,289; variance £79,289 overspend

findings.headline: HRA Planned Asset Management forecast at £48,715,663 against a revised budget of £57,588,527, and HRA New Build forecast at £6,727,112 against £13,669,505
findings.detail: Planned asset management had £7,664,462 spent to end Q2 and a forecast underspend of £8,872,864. HRA New Build had £422,674 spent to end Q2 and a forecast underspend of £6,942,394. Together with the affordable housing schemes, these lines make up the HRA forecast underspend.

findings.detail: Spend to end Q2 was £4,856,686, which is already close to the revised budget. The forecast of £7,635,903 is above budget, and the table records the variance as a £2,090,583 overspend.
findings.matters: A forecast overspend on a single HRA new-build scheme, set against an HRA programme that is otherwise forecast to underspend, is the kind of cost pressure a finance officer elsewhere would want to compare with their own new-build projects.
findings.figures: Revised budget £5,545,320; actual to end Q2 £4,856,686; forecast £7,635,903; variance £2,090,583 overspend

findings.matters: A finance director or lender tracking HRA borrowing and delivery would see roughly 31% of the HRA capital budget not forecast to be spent this year, which affects the timing of borrowing and funding need.

findings.detail: The Medium Term Financial Plan presented at budget setting identified an unresolved gap of £8.457m for 2027/28-2028/29 under base case assumptions, rising to £28.712m in worst-case scenarios. The council states that demand and cost growth are exceeding available resources in several key service areas. Key unresolved pressures include ALN, social care, temporary accommodation and home to school transport.
findings.matters: An unresolved MTFP gap of £8.457m over two years indicates the council's underlying revenue budget is unsustainable and raises questions about whether it can remain solvent without reserve depletion or service reductions.

findings.detail: Adult social care is experiencing major demand pressures: residential care overspending by £3.235m and support for children with disabilities by £0.603m, while children's services face £0.402m pressure from increased looked-after children numbers. findings.matters: Demand-led cost growth that outpaces available resources is structural and harder to control than input inflation; if demand pressures persist as forecast, reserves will deplete faster than planned.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Medium-term funding gap of £8.457m for next two years, worst case £28.7m
findings.detail: The Medium Term Financial Plan identifies a cumulative budget gap of £8.457m for 2027/28–2028/29 under base case assumptions. Under the 'worst case' scenario (higher inflation, lower council tax growth, lower external finance), the gap widens to £28.712m in 2028/29 alone. The council recognizes that 'current trends indicate that underlying demand and cost growth are exceeding available resources in several key service areas', particularly Additional Learning Needs, Social Care, Temporary Accommodation and Home to School Transport.
findings.matters: A structural funding gap of £8.5m+ cannot be closed by one-off savings alone. It implies material service reductions or significant use of reserves are inevitable within the planning horizon, both of which affect financial resilience and the council's credit rating from a lender's perspective.
findings.quote: The risk of future funding levels keeping pace with demand and inflationary pressures will increase the risk of further service reductions, reduced financial resilience and growing pressures on the Council's ability to maintain service delivery and statutory responsibilities.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation overspend persisting despite transformation savings target
findings.detail: Housing is forecasting £0.257m overspend in temporary accommodation despite a £0.150m saving target. This reflects 'sustained demand and wider national pressures'. Additionally, the Housing Benefit subsidy recovery rate has been revised downward from 20% to 16%, reducing income from these placements. Various mitigation measures are in progress (closure of out-of-county facility, new bed spaces created, security contract reviews) but their combined effect is insufficient to offset demand.
findings.matters: Sustained homelessness demand is a structural problem, not a cyclical one. The unfavorable change in Housing Benefit subsidy recovery removes a funding source and suggests the income position was optimistic in budget setting.
findings.figures: £0.257m overspend forecast, Housing Benefit subsidy recovery reduced from 20% to 16%
findings.quote: Housing is projecting an overspend of £0.257m which is predominantly from an increased spend forecast for Temporary Accommodation reflecting sustained demand and wider national pressures.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Teachers' pay award funding uncertain; Welsh Government considering unfunded increase from September 2026
findings.detail: The Cabinet Minister has consulted on a 3.5% pay award for teachers and school leaders (5% for unqualified staff) with an undertaking that additional funding would be provided to local authorities. However, this differs from the Independent Welsh Pay Review Body recommendation of 4.25% for all pay ranges, which the Cabinet Minister stated is 'not affordable within existing budgets'. The funding position remains unconfirmed as of June 2026.
findings.matters: Teacher pay is a material budget item. An unfunded pay award or shortfall in Welsh Government funding would create immediate pressure on the already-strained education budget.
findings.figures: Consultation underway on 3.5% teachers/school leaders and 5% unqualified staff vs 4.25% IWPRB recommendation
findings.quote: Uncertainty remains linked to the Teachers pay award from September 2026, this followed a written statement from Anna Brychan MS, the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language, that she would consult on a 3.5% pay award for teachers and school leaders and a 5% increase for unqualified teachers. The statement did advise that additional funding would be provided to local authorities.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Social care demand extremely volatile with strong overshoots already emerging
findings.detail: Adult services is forecasting £0.709m overspend driven entirely by demand: £3.235m additional cost for residential care placements and £0.603m for children with disabilities. Children's services has £0.908m pressure from looked-after children (£0.402m), loss of asylum seeker funding (£0.245m), and care leaver support (£0.261m). The paper warns demand 'can be extremely volatile, which could affect costs significantly by the end of the financial year'.
findings.matters: Social care is a statutory service where councils cannot refuse demand. Cost volatility of this magnitude creates material budget risk and constrains the council's ability to manage in-year financial pressures.
findings.figures: Adult services £0.709m overspend (from demand), comprising £3.235m residential care and £0.603m children with disabilities; Children's services £0.908m pressure
findings.quote: Members will be aware that demand for both children's and adults' social care can be extremely volatile, which could affect costs significantly by the end of the financial year.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: School budget deficits deteriorating and forecast to worsen significantly
findings.detail: The collective school deficit position has worsened to £4.358m projected by mid-year (from £4.526m budgeted), affecting 23 primary schools, 7 secondary schools and 1 middle school. The paper explicitly warns that 'current forecasts indicate that school deficits will increase significantly over the coming years'. The root causes are falling pupil numbers, surplus capacity, and growing Additional Learning Needs demand.
findings.matters: School deficits represent unfinanced obligations on the council's general fund. The structural nature of this problem (falling rolls, fixed costs) means it will not self-correct and will require either capital investment in estate consolidation or revenue transfers to schools from the general fund.
findings.figures: Collective school deficit £4.358m projected, comprising primary surplus £1.724m offset by secondary/middle/special deficit of £6.082m
findings.quote: The continuing deterioration in school balances highlights the need to address underlying structural pressures within the education system.

findings.detail: Of the £12.332m approved savings, £2.047m (16.6%) is assessed as RED with significant deliverability risk and £0.619m (5%) is AMBER with some risk. This means 21.6% of the savings programme—nearly a quarter of the total—is currently forecast not to be achieved. These undelivered savings would add to the £2.867m overspend already identified.
findings.matters: If savings do not land, the year-end outturn will be substantially worse than £2.867m. A lender needs to know whether this reported overspend is the full picture or whether it could grow materially as the year progresses.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Outturn Report For 2025/26.
findings.headline: Capital programme slippage and reserve use deferred external borrowing; Capital Financing Requirement of £343.4m exceeds actual debt of £272.2m by £71.2m
findings.detail: The council originally forecast it would need to undertake external borrowing in 2025/26, but capital programme delays, use of reserves, and cashflow management meant no external borrowing occurred. The council explicitly maintained cash surpluses to subsidise the capital programme and delay borrowing. The Capital Financing Requirement (£343.391m) significantly exceeds debt outstanding (£272.173m), indicating substantial capital funding needs are currently being met from cash reserves rather than through planned borrowing.
findings.matters: Deferring borrowing by drawing cash reserves is a short-term financing strategy that masks underlying capital requirements and depletes financial flexibility. While reducing near-term debt servicing costs, it defers the full cost of capital financing and suggests future borrowing needs will emerge as reserves are exhausted. Capital delays also extend service delivery timelines.
findings.figures: CFR £343.391m; total debt £272.173m; shortfall of £71.218m; originally forecast borrowing requirement did not materialize
findings.quote: For 2025/26 we had originally forecast that we would need to undertake borrowing, however due to slippage on the capital programme, use of reserves and cashflow , we have not needed to do this.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management and Capital Financing Prudential Indicators Outturn Report For 2025/26.
findings.headline: LOBO refinancing risk crystallized: FMS Wertmanagement rate spiked 292bp from 4.45% to 7.36%; council repaid to avoid future exposure
findings.detail: During 2025/26, the council's £10m LOBO loan with FMS Wertmanagement had its interest rate increased from 4.45% to 7.36% at the lender's option. The council exercised its option to repay the loan at no additional cost rather than accept the new terms. One remaining LOBO of £10m at 4.5% (3.7% of total debt portfolio) remains exposed to future rate changes at the lender's discretion.
findings.matters: LOBO loans shift refinancing risk to the council—lenders can force the authority to either accept higher rates or repay. A 292 basis point spike demonstrates the volatility in market-rate debt and the immediate impact on debt servicing costs when rates are reset.
findings.figures: FMS LOBO £10m repaid; rate increase from 4.45% to 7.36%; remaining LOBO £10m at 4.5% representing 3.7% of £272.173m debt
findings.quote: FMS Wertmanagement proposed to increase the interest rate on this loan from 4.45% to 7.36%. As a result, we decided to repay this loan at no additional cost as accepting the revised terms would mean the Authority would still have refinancing risk for the loan in later years .

findings.headline: Llanfabon School budget increased after market testing identified additional groundworks

findings.detail: New governance structure with strengthened oversight and gateway process created to implement recommendations from Audit Wales review of capital planning across Welsh authorities, signalling prior governance weaknesses.

findings.detail: Phase 1 works exceeded approved budget due to emergency defects discovered during construction, extending delivery from 5 weeks to 12 weeks. findings.headline: School PFI contract voluntary termination proceeding with additional costs; full implications pending

External advisor costs have been incurred in 2025/26, with the report noting 'A further report will be presented to Council in due course setting out the full financial implications, including termination costs, value for money considerations and potential revenue savings.'
findings.matters: PFI termination can involve significant one-off costs and also ongoing changes to service delivery arrangements. The council has not yet fully quantified the financial impact, representing a contingent liability.
